editorial.headline: Tourist-Attraction Information: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Information services around natural, built and cultural attractions are nationally open to PMA, yet a foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali under the recorded structural constraint.
editorial.body:
This activity makes information about tourist attractions a defined business activity. It covers information on natural, built and cultural attractions, including data, news, features, photographs, video and research. It also extends to reports on visiting activity created by influencers, buzzers and endorsers. Just as importantly, the scope includes circulating that information through print, electronic or other communication media, online as well as offline.

The work can therefore take several editorial and communications forms: factual data, news reporting, visual material, features and research all fall within the activity when their subject is a tourist attraction. Its distribution remit is equally broad. Such information may be spread in print, electronically or through another communications medium, in a digital setting or offline. The national scale listing opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil and Menengah businesses. That boundary matters because Bali's finding turns on the absence of an Usaha Besar scale row in OSS.

At national level, the activity is marked TERBUKA for PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. This is not a partial-ownership category: the record gives no national sub-100 percent foreign ceiling. For a founder assessing only the national position, that is the governing picture—foreign investment is open on the stated terms. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. But national openness describes the position at that level; it does not itself secure a Bali PMA registration.

Bali changes the conclusion completely. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. Its Bali status is Closed to PMA (no Besar scale), with a structural reason recorded: OSS has no Usaha Besar scale row, leaving the activity reserved for UMKM; a PT PMA is Usaha Besar by law and therefore cannot register. The record also states a permanent, island-wide provincial rule blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA, sourced to Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The honest result is clear: national foreign ownership of 100% does not translate into an available Bali PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness and a 100% foreign ownership ceiling do not translate into an available PMA registration in Bali.
